data.text: Council convened on: "Treasury Yields Push To Fresh Highs" (WSJ, published 04 Oct 2026 04:40 UTC). Blind votes are in; members, make your case.
Surging Treasury yields pressure rate-sensitive sectors like property and financials, while technology shows resilience despite the broader bond market selloff.
The US 10-year Treasury yield has surged, rising 10.03% over the past month to 5.277%.
Rising yields have severely impacted rate-sensitive sectors, with Property down 6.68% and Financials down 7.23% over the last month.
Despite rising yields, the Technology sector has remained strong, gaining 8.83% over the past month.
The broader S&P 500 has managed a slight gain of 0.73% over the past month, masking underlying sector divergence.
The US Dollar Index has strengthened by 2.38% over the past month, reflecting higher yields and attracting capital flows.

data.text: Higher Treasury yields pressure Japan property and technology while financials and the yen stay mixed.
The Nikkei 225 fell 0.94% on the day, though it is still up 3.01% over one month.
USD/JPY was nearly flat at 157.83, down 0.06% on the day and up 1.39% over one month.
The property proxy is the weakest sector, down 6.34% over one month.
Financials fell 3.7% over one month, so higher yields have not lifted bank shares.
A global bond sell-off already pushed Japanese stocks lower through borrowing costs, and Treasury yields have since hit fresh highs.
Challenge to BEAR: A strongly bearish Japan financials call overstates the pack: shares are down 3.7% over one month, not collapsing, and the yen barely moved.
Challenge to SPILLOVER: A neutral Japan technology view misses a 7.19% one-month gain with 47.24% volatility, leaving multiples exposed to higher yields.

data.plain_english: Borrowing costs in the United States have climbed to new highs. The council expects businesses that depend on cheap loans, especially property companies in the US, Hong Kong and Japan, and Hong Kong technology firms, to struggle more. US technology companies have held up well so far and may keep doing better, though the council is not confident. Members disagree most about Japanese technology companies, which have risen recently but could be hurt if borrowing costs keep climbing. This is research to help you think, not advice to buy or sell.
